subject: English
passage: Independent bookshops have long been a fixture of the Cedar Hill district, where modest storefront rents historically discouraged larger commercial tenants. As the neighborhood has gentrified over the past decade, however, national chain cafes have proliferated along its main corridors. It has been proposed that rent increases in gentrifying districts can benefit chain establishments more than local independents; to evaluate this possibility, sociologists Ngozi Benali and Eleanor Ingram tracked independent bookshops and chain cafes, along with other local and chain businesses, across several years, concluding that chain establishments are advantaged by rising commercial rents in Cedar Hill.
prompt: Which finding, if true, would most directly support Benali and Ingram's conclusion?

choices.A: Although independent bookshops and chain cafes tended to expand their operating hours by similar amounts in years with stable rents, chain cafes reduced their operating hours more sharply than independent bookshops did in years with steep rent increases.
choices.B: Although independent bookshops and chain cafes both tended to expand their floor space in years with steep rent increases, the expansion was much greater for chain cafes than for independent bookshops.
choices.C: Although independent bookshops and chain cafes both tended to report higher annual revenues in years with steep rent increases than they did in years with stable rents, the years with steep rent increases also coincided with a surge in local tourism.
choices.D: Although significant year-to-year variations in commercial rent levels were observed during the study, neither chain cafes nor independent bookshops showed any significant year-to-year variation in their rates of floor space expansion.

explanation:
Choice B is the best answer because it presents a finding that, if true, would most directly support Benali and Ingram's conclusion that chain establishments are advantaged by rising commercial rents in Cedar Hill. The passage explains that the sociologists tracked both independent bookshops (the local type) and chain cafes (the chain type) across several years to evaluate whether rent increases benefit chains more than local independents. A finding that both business types expanded their floor space in years with steep rent increases, but that the expansion was much greater for chain cafes than for independent bookshops, would support the conclusion that chains are advantaged by such conditions. A greater expansion would give chain cafes a clear comparative advantage over independent bookshops when commercial rents rise.

Why A is incorrect:

Choice A is incorrect because a finding that chain cafes reduced their operating hours more sharply than independent bookshops did in years with steep rent increases would contradict rather than support Benali and Ingram's conclusion. If chain cafes fared worse than independent bookshops when rents rose, this would suggest that independent bookshops, not chain cafes, benefited more from rising commercial rents.
